SOURCE EXCERPT:
The university's conflict-of-interest disclosure is filed annually by every investigator on a sponsored award and updated within thirty days of any new interest. A significant financial interest means anything of value received from a single entity exceeding five thousand dollars in the preceding twelve months, or any equity in a non-publicly-traded entity regardless of value. Income from seminars or teaching sponsored by a federal or state agency, or by an institution of higher education, is excluded from the threshold. The Conflict Review Committee determines whether a disclosed interest relates to the investigator's research, and only a related interest requires a management plan. Management plans are reviewed annually and made available to the sponsoring agency on request. An investigator who fails to disclose is removed from the award until the committee has reviewed the interest, and the department chair is notified in writing.
